title: Kepler to Müller, 2 September 1630
author: Johannes Kepler
source: Johannes Kepler's letter to Philipp Müller written at Lauban on 2 September 1630, sent with Friedrich Bartsch to see to the sale of the *Ephemerides*, and defending the title he had given Wallenstein, as Duke of Mecklenburg, in their dedication. It is the last of Kepler's letters to Müller in the collection; Kepler died at Regensburg two months later. The original is lost; the copy is in the Bibliothèque de l'Observatoire, Paris (B, 1, 9 (89); 89, 8. L). First printed in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 78–79.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Kepler sends Friedrich Bartsch to see to the sale of the *Ephemerides* and defends giving Wallenstein his title as Duke of Mecklenburg in the dedication. His last letter to Müller; he died at Regensburg two months later.

notes.note: Wallenstein, Kepler's patron, was invested by the Emperor with the duchy of Mecklenburg in 1629, after its dukes were deposed for siding with Denmark. The dedication of the *Ephemerides* calls him Duke of Mecklenburg.

The see of Magdeburg was disputed: its chapter had chosen August, son of the Elector of Saxony, while the Emperor sought it, with Halberstadt, for his son Archduke Leopold Wilhelm. Kepler would give either claimant the title in use.
